# Wave Laser fires from ship

## Headline

The beam weapons (Wave Laser and Mining Laser — both confirmed in scope, Q1 = A) currently render a **static polyline frozen at fire time**, so as the ship keeps flying during the beam's visible lifetime the beam's source end visibly detaches from the ship. The fix: each frame the beam's **source end tracks the ship's current position** while its **destination (the launch-resolved end point) stays fixed** — a purely visual change in the shared VFX seam.

## Problem statement

When the ship fires a beam weapon and keeps moving, the rendered beam stays anchored to the world position the ship occupied at the moment of firing rather than to the ship itself. With the ship's max speed around 175 px/s, a Wave Laser beam (visible 0.3 s) can drift up to ~50 px clear of the ship's nose while the beam is still on screen, so the beam visibly no longer "fires from the ship". The Mining Laser beam (visible 0.12 s) has the same static-polyline behaviour and is confirmed in scope (Q1 = A).

## Users

- **The player** — watches the ship fire the Wave Laser (and Mining Laser) while dodging; the beam should read as emanating from the ship's current position, never as floating in space where the ship was a moment ago.

**User stories:**

- As the player, when my ship fires a Wave Laser and I keep flying, the red beam's source end stays attached to my ship and follows it, while the beam's far end stays fixed at the point where it resolved — so the beam always visibly fires *from* my ship.
- As the player, when the Mining Laser is cutting an asteroid, its beam likewise stays connected to my ship as it drifts, not detached at the position where the shot was fired.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — **Source follows the ship (Wave Laser).** During the Wave Laser beam's visible lifetime, its rendered source end re-anchors each frame to the ship's current position, so the beam stays visibly connected to the ship as it moves.
- AC2 — **Destination stays fixed.** The beam's far end remains at the launch-resolved destination — the first-intercept point when the ray met an entity, otherwise the full-extent endpoint — for the beam's whole visible life. The beam is never re-aimed or re-resolved: no damage is re-applied, no hit is recomputed, and the ray's damage result stays exactly as resolved at launch.
- AC3 — **Wrapped path preserved.** As the ship moves, the beam is redrawn along the **shortest wrapped path** from the ship's current position to the fixed destination (one segment per arena-edge crossing), consistent with the existing wrapped-segment geometry used by the Mining Laser beam.
- AC4 — **Duration, fade and cleanup unchanged.** The beam keeps its configured visible duration (0.3 s Wave Laser), fades and destroys identically, and never persists past its lifetime; the per-frame redraw stays cheap (a single Graphics, delta-driven, following the existing self-cleaning beam pattern).
- AC5 — **Game↔gym parity.** The re-anchoring lives in the shared VFX seam and the shared fire path (`CombatCoreScene.fireHitscanBeam`), so `PlayScene` and every gym render the identical tracking beam; the duplicate-body guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` still passes.
- AC6 — **Mining Laser re-anchors too.** The Mining Laser beam re-anchors its source the same way: each frame its source end tracks the ship's current position while its destination (the target asteroid's position **frozen at fire time**) stays fixed; the change must not regress the Mining Laser's damage, target selection or cadence (`CombatScene.onMiningLaserFire` still damages the selected live asteroid exactly once per shot, and the beam does **not** track the asteroid as it drifts).
- AC7 — **Tests and documentation.** Unit tests cover: a moving ship re-anchors the beam source while the destination never moves; no re-hit or re-damage occurs during the beam's life; the wrapped path updates when the ship crosses an arena edge mid-beam; and game↔gym parity. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries (e.g. `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` only if a divergence is retained). The full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

As a player, the Wave Laser (and Mining Laser) beam now visibly emanates from your ship and stays attached as you fly, instead of floating in the space your ship occupied a moment ago.

## Constraints

- **Visual-only change.** Aim (per-shot RNG bias), cadence, damage and hit resolution are already settled at launch and must not change; the beam never re-hits or re-damages.
- **Shared seam.** The behaviour must live once in `src/scenes/core/` + `src/vfx/` so the game and every gym (GymWeapons, GymMinerals) run the same code — per the gym↔game parity convention (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).
- **Cheap by construction.** The Mining Laser fires up to once per sixteenth note (~0.1875 s); a per-frame redraw must not accumulate Graphics objects or tweens and must clean itself up on expiry and scene shutdown.
- **Ship reference lifecycle.** The beam outlives the launch frame; it must resolve the ship's position through a safe provider that survives the ship being destroyed or the scene shutting down mid-beam.

## Existing state

- **Wave Laser** is an **instant hitscan ray** (AH-0MVREBUJ5004HDRQ): `CombatCoreScene.fireHitscanBeam` resolves the ray once at launch (`resolveHitscanRay` in `src/scenes/core/hitscanBeam.ts`), applies exactly 1 damage at the first intercept through the shared kill seam, and renders the static polyline with `spawnHitscanBeam` (`src/vfx/hitscanBeam.ts`) — a red column with white-hot core, faded via a 0.3 s tween. The beam geometry is frozen at the launch muzzle position.
- **Mining Laser** fires an instant beam from the ship to the selected asteroid: `CombatScene.onMiningLaserFire` calls `spawnMiningLaserBeam` (`src/vfx/miningLaserBeam.ts`), which draws a static wrapped polyline from the **fire-time** ship position to the **fire-time** target position and ages it over 0.12 s via a delta-driven update. This module already owns the wrapped shortest-path helper (`miningLaserBeamSegments`) that the anchored beam would share.
- Both beams are therefore disconnected from the ship for the rest of their visible life once the ship moves — exactly the reported defect.

## Desired change

- Extend the beam VFX seam with an **anchored-beam renderer**: instead of drawing a one-shot static polyline, the beam Graphics takes a **source provider** (a function returning the ship's current position, or a scene method like `getPlayer()`) plus a **fixed destination** point, and on each frame recomputes the wrapped shortest path (`miningLaserBeamSegments`-style, from `src/vfx/miningLaserBeam.ts`) between the current source and the fixed destination, clearing and redrawing the Graphics. Duration, fade, registry and shutdown cleanup stay as today.
- `CombatCoreScene.fireHitscanBeam` passes the player as the source anchor and `resolution.end` as the fixed destination (the intercept point, or the full-extent endpoint when nothing was intercepted).
- `CombatScene.onMiningLaserFire` snapshots the target position at fire time (freezing the destination — the beam does **not** track the asteroid as it drifts, per "destination stays fixed") and passes the player as the source anchor.

## Key Files:

- `src/vfx/hitscanBeam.ts` — Wave Laser beam VFX: replace the static-polyline draw with the per-frame source-following anchored render (source provider + fixed destination), keeping duration/fade/registry semantics.
- `src/vfx/miningLaserBeam.ts` — home of the wrapped shortest-path helper (`miningLaserBeamSegments`) the anchored beam reuses; Mining Laser beam gets the same treatment (confirmed in scope, Q1 = A).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — `fireHitscanBeam`: pass the player anchor + `resolution.end` to the renderer.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `onMiningLaserFire`: freeze the target position at fire time and pass the player anchor.
- `src/scenes/core/hitscanBeam.ts` — ray geometry (unchanged; supplies the fixed destination via the existing `resolution.end`).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — parity guard that must still pass unchanged.
- Tests (new/updated): `src/vfx/hitscanBeam.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.test.ts`, `src/vfx/miningLaserBeam.test.ts`, plus any gym test that exercises the beam while the ship moves.

## Related work

- AH-0MVREBUJ5004HDRQ (completed, v0.1.18) — **Wave laser redesign**: built the hitscan beam seam (`src/scenes/core/hitscanBeam.ts`, `src/vfx/hitscanBeam.ts`) that this item now makes ship-tracking.
- AH-0MW9QMP2P0032BWW (completed, v0.1.21) — **Shared core mining-laser fire step**: the shared `CombatCoreScene._updateMiningLaser` / `CombatScene.onMiningLaserFire` fire path the Mining Laser change would extend.
- AH-0MW9QMQ7B005WFH9 (completed, v0.1.21) — **Mining-laser beam VFX and audio cue**: the `spawnMiningLaserBeam` renderer and its wrapped-segment helper.
- AH-0MW9QMSI7005UU9P (completed) — **Gym coverage and parity for the mining laser** (GymMinerals), the parity gym for the Mining Laser half.
- AH-0MW10J31B0053E56 (completed) — **Wave Laser tuning**: level-resolved ray length/aim bias that fixes the level-0 length at 240 px.
- AH-0MV5DFBVW002J2XO (completed) — **Orbital Fires in direction of orb**: precedent for re-anchoring a fired effect's origin to a moving source object.

## Risks & assumptions

- **R1 — Beam pivot feel.** With a near intercept and the ship moving fast, the re-anchored beam pivots noticeably around its fixed destination, which may look unusual up close. Mitigation: source-anchor to the ship's natural firing point (the same position the ray resolved from); verify feel in the weapons gym before review.
- **R2 — Per-frame redraw cost.** The Mining Laser can fire every ~0.1875 s; a per-frame beam redraw must stay a single Graphics redraw with no object or tween accumulation. Mitigation: reuse the existing delta-driven, self-cleaning beam lifecycle and clear/redraw in place.
- **R3 — Ship destroyed mid-beam.** The beam outlives the launch frame, so the source provider must be safe if the ship is destroyed or the scene shuts down mid-life. Mitigation: provider guards against a missing player plus the existing shutdown cleanup.
- **R4 — Scope creep.** Re-aiming the beam at a moving enemy, tracking moving destinations, applying source-tracking to other weapons, or touching damage/aim/cadence are **out of scope**; any such opportunity should be recorded as a linked work item, not added to this change.

## Assumptions

- **A1 — Visual-only.** The beam's source tracking is a rendering change; the ray still resolves once at launch and damage, aim and cadence are untouched. Re-resolution or re-hits would contradict "destination stays fixed" and are out of scope.
- **A2 — Destination frozen at launch.** The beam's far end is the launch-resolved end point (first-intercept point, or full-extent endpoint) and stays there for the beam's whole visible life, even if the intercepted entity or anything else moves.
- **A3 — Mining Laser in scope** (confirmed by the producer: Q1 = A). The Mining Laser beam's destination is frozen at fire time — it does **not** follow the asteroid as it drifts; only the source re-anchors to the ship.

## Open Questions

- **RESOLVED Q1 — Is the Mining Laser in scope?** Producer answer: **A — yes, include the Mining Laser.** The Mining Laser beam has the identical static-polyline defect (0.12 s visible, ship up to ~21 px clear), and once the anchored-beam renderer exists the incremental cost is small. AC6 now mandates the same source-follows-ship treatment with the destination frozen at fire time.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-16 — Intake draft created from the seed description (auto-dispatched). Scope, ACs, key files and the single open scope question (Q1) recorded; duplicate check performed (no overlapping item found).
- 2026-11-16 — Producer answered Q1 = **A (Mining Laser in scope)**. AC6 rewritten as a firm criterion (destination frozen at fire time, no asteroid-tracking), headline/desired-change/key-files updated, the Open Question marked RESOLVED, and the Appendix records the answer.
- 2026-11-16 — Plan auto-complete (plan skill, Process step 1): the item is a bug (not an epic) whose description already carries measurable ACs (AC1–AC7) and a minimal implementation sketch (anchored-beam renderer + source provider + fixed destination, key files, constraints, risks). Effort Small / risk Medium just misses the auto-skip threshold (which requires risk Low), so the plan pre-check routed to the Process — but planning adds no value here; no decomposition into child features. AC-coverage review: `proceed` (no children, no conflicts). Decision recorded; item advanced to `plan_complete`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (asked as part of this intake): "Is the Mining Laser in scope for the source-follows-ship beam change?" — Answer (producer, 2026-11-16): **A — yes, include the Mining Laser.** Final: A (Option A — include), as recommended. Source: producer reply to the handoff comment AH-C0MWJAAJH80067EGM on the work item; research: both beams render a static polyline frozen at fire time and visibly detach from the ship (Wave Laser 0.3 s visible / ~50 px at max speed; Mining Laser 0.12 s / ~21 px), and one shared anchored-beam renderer covers both.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTV7OAJM002GGMM** – Move control buttons for gym scenes to the bottom (completed)
- **AH-0MUZMTS8J0029FSS** – Add figure-of-8 boss movement in shared core (completed)
- **AH-0MV1EDVNF004MTYN** – Wave laser audio fire/pickup cues and leveling-gym round-robin (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: destination, fires, fixed, laser, mining, move, moves, needs, origin, point, possibly, ship, source, stays, wave
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — matched: destination, fires, fixed, laser, mining, move, moves, needs, origin, point, ship, source, stays, wave
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: destination, fires, fixed, laser, mining, move, moves, needs, origin, point, ship, source, stays, wave

# Test runner crashes with UnboundLocalError when a full-scope suite resolves to no commands

## Problem Statement

`run_tests.py` crashes with `UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'state_changed_flag'` when a named suite resolves to zero commands. Instead of reporting the empty resolution gracefully, the function references a variable that was never bound.

## Users

- Agent sessions that run the test skill with a named suite (e.g. `--suite node`) that happens to resolve to no commands in the current repo.
- CI / automation that invokes the test runner with varying suites across repositories.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A full-scope run whose suite resolves to no commands completes without an `UnboundLocalError` — either with an actionable message naming the suite and resolution path, or a clean early return with a zero-command report.
2. The `state_changed_flag` variable is initialised before the command-execution loop (or the loop body guard handles the empty case), so the post-loop aggregation path never touches an unbound variable.
3. A regression test exercises the zero-command path (mocking `commands` to an empty list, or using a suite name that resolves to nothing) and asserts no crash.

## Impact

Users running the test runner against a suite with zero commands get a clear, actionable error message instead of an obscure Python `UnboundLocalError` crash.

## Constraints

- Fix is in a shared skill (`run_tests.py` in the `test` skill scripts); changes must not break existing callers.
- The existing `state_changed_flag` semantics (mid-run checkout movement tracking) must be preserved for the normal non-empty command path.

## Existing State

`run_tests.py` initialises `state_changed_flag` inside the `for cmd in commands:` loop body (line 3188). After the loop, the function reads `state_changed_flag` on line 3281 to populate `state_changed_during_run` in the result dict. When `commands` is empty, the loop body never executes, leaving the name unbound.

## Key Files

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — Move `state_changed_flag` initialisation before the `for cmd in commands:` loop (line ~3183, after `slot_waits`).
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/tests/` — Add regression test for the zero-command path.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep:** The fix is narrowly scoped to the `UnboundLocalError`. Do not refactor other loop-scoped variables (e.g. `command_waits`, `command_elapsed`) unless they show the same pattern.
- **Assumption:** Moving the initialisation before the loop is safe — `state_changed_flag` is reset per-command inside the loop for the normal case. We should verify whether a per-iteration reset is actually needed or whether a single pre-loop initialisation suffices.
- **Risk:** If `state_changed_flag` is intentionally per-command (reset for each iteration), a single pre-loop initialisation may lose the reset semantics. The fix should preserve per-command reset only if the logic requires it; otherwise the pre-loop init is sufficient.

## Related Work

- Discovered from AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2 ("Bot oscillates too much") — the agent was running the test skill during implementation and hit this crash.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Does `state_changed_flag` need per-command reset, or is a single pre-loop initialisation sufficient?" — Answer (Map): A pre-loop initialisation to `None` is sufficient. The per-command reassignment on line 3224 (`state_changed_flag = run.get("state_changed_during_run")`) overwrites the value each iteration; the post-loop read (line 3281) captures the last iteration's value (or `None` if zero iterations). The bug is simply that the declaration line never runs when the loop body is skipped.

# Weapon evolutions: fuse two active weapon kinds into an evolved weapon

Discovered from the 2026-11-17 gameplay-mechanics review (rank 8 of 10;
direction: create, **Medium** priority).

## Problem statement

The sixteen catalogue weapons are independent: nothing in
`src/utils/weapons.ts`, the shared fire path or the catalogue data reads a
*combination* of two active kinds. A run takes about **two** upgrades (GDD §2.7
target `upgradesSelected 2.00 ± 0.50`), each timed weapon lasts 10 s
(`WEAPON_EFFECT_DURATION`), and the hold-full choice offers level-ups of a
single kind — so a run's build rarely reads as more than "Cannon plus Spread",
and mixing two weapons pays no premium over stacking one.

## Users

A player building a loadout during a run, and — secondarily — the designer
authoring pairings and the gym that must demonstrate them.

- As a player mid-run, I want the second weapon I collect to sometimes **fuse**
  with my first into a visibly different weapon, so my pickups add up to an
  identity I chose rather than a longer list of guns.
- As a player, I want to learn the recipes from play, so I can plan ("I need one
  more `arc` for Chain Ricochet") instead of reading a wiki.
- As a designer, I want pairings to be declarative data with a validating test,
  so a new pairing is a content unit and a typo fails loudly.
- As a gym user, I want a gym row that fires every shipped pairing through the
  same code the game runs, so parity is demonstrable and not asserted.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **One pure resolver.** A pure pairing resolver (new module beside
   `src/utils/weapons.ts`) answers, for the active/owned weapon set, which
   evolved weapon (if any) is live and why (field overlap vs owned pair). No
   scene, gym or bot-decision module derives its own answer.
2. **Pairings are catalogue data with a validating test.** An unknown weapon id
   in a pairing fails loudly at load/validation time; a catalogue without
   pairing data reproduces today's behaviour byte-for-byte (no pairing ⇒ no
   evolved weapon, identical firing trace).
3. **Field tier (timed overlap).** While both kinds of a pairing are active
   simultaneously the evolved pattern fires; when either half expires the
   evolved weapon stops on the next bar downbeat and each half reverts to its
   own pattern.
4. **Owned tier (permanent).** Once both kinds are permanently owned at level
   ≥ 2 — through the shipped hold-full grants, the hangar buy-to-upgrade levels
   (`MAX_PERMANENT_LEVEL = 5`, base 1), or both — the evolved weapon persists for
   the rest of the run and survives the expiry of a timed overlap; `reset`/
   run restart clears it exactly as it clears other owned weapons.
5. **Damage parity.** An automated comparison shows an evolved weapon produces
   no more damage instances per cadence tick than the two halves it replaces,
   and the boss still requires 200 hits at every weapon level.
6. **Grid conformance.** Every evolved cadence resolves to whole 16th-note
   onsets at `beatBpm` on the shared lattice, and pattern morphs occur only on
   bar downbeats.
7. **Legibility.** Fusion and expiry each read through a distinct cue, a HUD
   badge naming the evolved weapon plus its icon, with a shape/text difference
   that does not rely on colour alone; cues respect the shared SFX settings.
8. **Gym ↔ game parity.** `GymWeapons` (or a dedicated row) fires every shipped
   pairing through the shared code path, with a row in `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.
9. **Determinism.** Same seed and input trace produce the same firing trace.
10. **Balance evidence.** A same-seed bot batch shows `survivalSeconds`,
    `levelReached` and `avoidableHits` inside the experience-target bands, and
    the ring-timing harness is re-measured (a fusion that shortens ring 1 below
    its window is a tuning input, not a blocker). The level-0 output budget
    (non-cannon weapons ≤ 60 % of pre-change level-0 output, GDD §4.4.2) still
    holds.
11. **Hex matchup classification.** An evolved weapon resolves to its **base**
    weapon id(s) for hex matchup purposes, so a fusion can never bypass a hex's
    authored `strengths` / `weaknesses` (cross-item requirement from
    AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ); the resolver publishes both ids and a test pins the
    classification.
12. **Documentation.** GDD §4.4 gains the pairing table (and §8.3's "proposed,
    not shipped" entry is updated to shipped), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` gains the gym
    row, and a `src/weaponBalanceDocs.test.ts`-style docs test covers the
    pairing table so the document and the data cannot drift. Code comments are
    updated to reflect the changes, including README and any relevant wiki or
    docs-site entries.
13. **Test gate.** The full project test suite passes with the new changes
    (run through the test skill).

## Impact

A player who collects a second weapon that pairs with their first now sees the
two fuse into a named, visibly different weapon, so a run's pickups add up to a
build the player chose rather than a longer list of guns.

## Proposed mechanic (retained from the seed item)

1. **Pairings are catalogue data.** A declarative entry names, for a **pair** of
   weapon ids, the evolved weapon id. Pilot table (three authored pairings):
   - `ricochet` + `arc` → **Chain Ricochet** — bolts bank off walls *and* hop to
     a second nearby target on each bounce.
   - `cluster` + `mortar` → **Cluster Barrage** — MIRV warheads leave short
     lingering blasts at their burst points.
   - `spread` + `options` → **Fan Escort** — the orbiting pods fire along the
     ship's heading instead of radially, forming a wide fan.
2. **Two tiers, both earned in play (no new economy).** Field evolution fires
   for the overlap window of two active halves; permanent evolution persists
   once both halves are owned at level ≥ 2.
3. **Pattern, coverage and behaviour only** — never damage instances per shot.
4. **Cadence stays on the shared lattice** as its own `(k, n, rotation)` ladder,
   so an evolved weapon morphs only on a bar downbeat and stays phase-locked.
5. **Legibility**: a distinct fusion cue, a HUD badge with the evolved name and
   icon, and a matching downbeat cue on expiry.
6. **One pure module** consumed by the shared fire path, so the game and every
   weapon gym run identical code.

## Constraints and assumptions

- **No new economy and no new slot.** Evolutions consume the existing six
  shared slots and the existing hold-full / hangar level paths; nothing is
  purchasable.
- **Pattern, not power.** An evolution must not raise damage per tick or the
  number of damage instances; the balance risk is coverage, and AC5 pins it.
- **Authored, not combinatorial.** Three pairings ship; the mechanism supports
  more, but each pairing is a balance-tested content unit.
- **One resolver.** Pairing logic never appears in a scene, a gym or a
  bot-decision module — bot decisions read the resolved active set.
- **Permanent levels are one snapshot.** Both ownership sources (run hold-full
  grants, hangar buy-to-upgrade) already converge on `Player.getWeaponLevels()`;
  the owned tier reads that snapshot rather than adding persisted state.
- **No dependency on AH-0MWKT12BT001106T** (hangar power-up ownership) — that
  sibling gap is about power-ups' first permanent row, not weapons.
- **Assumption:** the evolved ids are resolved *output*, not new catalogue rows,
  so `src/data/weapons.csv` and `weaponCatalogueParity.test.ts` stay untouched
  (see Risks for the fallback if this proves wrong).

## Existing state (verified in the repo, 2026-11-17)

- **Catalogue ids**: the 16 ids are declared in `src/utils/weapons.ts:100`
  (`cannon, spread, dual, rapid, wave_laser, ricochet, cluster, options, nova,
  mortar, arc, rear_guard, broadside, railgun, shard_swarm, heavy_slug`).
  `WeaponDefinition` is at `src/utils/weapons.ts:810`; subdivision-based
  fire-rate constants (`WEAPON_*_FIRE_RATE`) derive cadence from the beat
  lattice, so an evolved weapon slots into the same shape.
- **`resolveWeaponDefinition`** is the one level-resolving catalogue read,
  consumed by `src/entities/Player.ts:1226`, `src/ai/eval/arena.ts:983` (bot
  arena) and `src/utils/weaponStrength.ts`. Any second resolution path would be
  a duplicate.
- **Catalogue data is CSV-authored**: `src/data/weapons.csv` (one row per
  weapon, header documents `id, name, description, subdivisions, bulletColor,
  bulletShape, bulletSize, …`), patterns in `src/data/weapon-patterns.csv`,
  ladder rungs in `src/data/weapon-levels.json` (`{k, n, rotation}` per level
  per weapon). Parsed by `parseWeaponCatalogue` (`src/core/csv.ts`), guarded at
  runtime by `src/utils/weaponCatalogue.ts`, written by
  `src/core/weaponCatalogueStore.ts`, and pinned by
  `src/data/weaponCatalogueParity.test.ts`.
- **The pairing relation is cross-row**, so it cannot live as a column in
  `weapons.csv` — it needs its own table wherever it is authored.
- **Shared fire path and active set**: `src/entities/Player.ts`
  (`getActiveWeapons()` `:896`, `_permanentWeapons` `:315`,
  `_permanentWeaponGrants` `:324`, `getWeaponLevels()` permanent-level
  snapshot), plus the region registry in `src/powerups/effects.ts`
  (`EffectsRegistry` `:361`, `WEAPON_EFFECT_DURATION = 10`,
  `src/powerups/effects.ts:159`).
- **Permanent level ladder already exists**: `MAX_PERMANENT_LEVEL = 5` with
  `BASE_PERMANENT_LEVEL = 1` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts:583`), so
  "owned at level ≥ 2" is reachable both in-run (two hold-full grants) and from
  the hangar (buy-to-upgrade, AH-0MWHW4ALS0039JFU, completed).
- **Ownership display** already reads the permanent-only snapshot:
  `buildOwnedLoadout` (`src/powerups/ownedLoadout.ts:97`) — the same snapshot the
  owned tier should read, so no new persistence is needed.
- **Drop feedback surfaces**: `src/powerups/icons.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.ts`
  and `src/ui/HUD.ts`.
- **Gyms**: `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts`, `GymWeaponLeveling`,
  `GymWeaponTuning`; the parity ledger `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` already documents
  the weapon rows (`:115`, `:116`).
- **Docs**: GDD §4.4 carries a "proposed, not shipped (backlog §8.3)" pointer to
  weapon evolutions (`docs/Game Design Document.md:1203`); §8.3 holds the
  backlog entry. The `*Docs.test.ts` convention (e.g.
  `src/weaponBalanceDocs.test.ts`) is how a document is pinned to its data.
- **Hex matchup does not exist yet**: no `resolveHexMatchup` symbol exists in
  `src/`; hex `strengths`/`weaknesses` live in
  `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` / `hexRing.ts` and the matchup resolver is
  still open work (AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ, `open`/`plan_complete`) — see Q3.

## Desired change

1. New pure module `src/utils/weaponEvolutions.ts` holding the authored pairing
   table and the resolver: input = active ids + permanent levels, output = the
   live evolved id (or none), its base ids, and the reason
   (`field` | `owned` | none).
2. Evolved definitions added beside the catalogue (id, name, icon, colour,
   pattern/ladder, cadence subdivision) resolving through the existing
   `Subdivisions`/`WEAPON_*_FIRE_RATE` shape so cadence stays on the lattice.
3. Exactly one call site in the shared fire path (`Player`/`CombatCoreScene`)
   reads the resolved set instead of enumerating weapons itself; the bot arena
   reads the same resolution.
4. Fusion/expiry feedback: cue + HUD badge (name, icon, shape/text, not
   colour-only) through the shared SFX settings.
5. Gym demonstration of every shipped pairing through the shared path, plus the
   `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` row.
6. Docs: pairing table in GDD §4.4, §8.3 entry promoted, docs test pinning the
   table, code comments updated.

## Key Files

- `src/utils/weaponEvolutions.ts` *(new)* — pairing table, evolved definitions,
  the pure resolver, and its unit tests (`weaponEvolutions.test.ts`).
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — `WeaponId` union extension for evolved ids (if the
  evolved ids join the union) and the shared `WeaponDefinition` shape.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — the single resolved-active-weapon read
  (`getActiveWeapons`, `_permanentWeaponGrants`, `getWeaponLevels`).
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — the shared region/auto-fire path the evolved
  pattern fires through.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts`, `src/ui/HUD.ts` — evolved icon and fusion badge.
- `src/data/weapon-levels.json` (or a sibling file) — evolved cadence rungs, if
  cadence is authored as data rather than constants.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` (+ tests) — the pairing parity row.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4, §8.3),
  `src/weaponBalanceDocs.test.ts`-style docs test.

## Risks and mitigations

- **Power creep through coverage.** Fusions widen coverage even at equal damage
  per tick. Mitigation: AC5's automated damage-instance comparison plus AC10's
  bot-batch bands; evolved cadence is a tuning input, not a free upgrade.
- **A second resolution path.** The obvious failure is a gym or scene deriving
  its own answer. Mitigation: AC1 forbids it and AC8's gym row fires the shared
  path, so a divergence shows up as a gym failure.
- **Phase drift on the lattice.** A bespoke timer would break the shared beat
  lattice. Mitigation: AC6 resolves evolved cadence to whole 16th-note onsets
  and morphs only on bar downbeats.
- **Owned-tier confusion.** Two ownership sources (run hold-full grants vs
  hangar permanent levels) could disagree. Mitigation: both are already one
  permanent snapshot (`Player.getWeaponLevels()`), which is what
  `buildOwnedLoadout` reads — reuse it rather than adding state.
- **Scope creep.** The mechanism invites more than three pairings, a fusion
  economy, or researched-weapon pairings from
  `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`. Those are follow-up work items, not
  scope here.
- **Assumption (verify at implementation).** Evolved ids can stay outside the
  `WeaponId` union (resolved output only) — this avoids touching the CSV parity
  test and the bot arena's `WeaponId` handling. If they must join the union, the
  CSV and parity tests need rows too.

## Related work

- GDD §2.3 (shared beat lattice), §4.4 (catalogue + level-0 output budget),
  §4.4.2 (weapon strength budget), §4.3 (boss 200-hit pool), §8.3 (backlog
  entry), §2.7 (`upgradesSelected` target).
- **AH-0MTV7RITM009LJF6** — Make weapons both cumulative and time out
  (completed): the timed-cumulative active set the field tier observes.
- **AH-0MUQOTSFE00462EJ** — Feature: per-weapon level state on Player
  (completed): `getWeaponLevels()` / `_permanentWeaponGrants`.
- **AH-0MUQOVYZU0073OUV** — Feature: permanent mineral-choice weapon leveling
  (completed): the hold-full path that raises the owned tier's level.
- **AH-0MWHW4ALS0039JFU** — Hangar UI: buy to upgrade owned weapons and power-ups
  (completed): the hangar permanent levels the owned tier reads.
- **AH-0MWKT12BT001106T** — Hangar power-up ownership: no path creates a
  power-up's first permanent level row (`open`): sibling work on the ownership
  model; this item must not depend on it.
- **AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ** — Make hex strengths and weaknesses matter in combat
  (`open`/`plan_complete`): source of the AC11 base-id requirement.
- `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` — the pairing layer is the natural
  home for future researched weapons.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

Answers pending — the three decisions below materially change scope,
authoring surface and sequencing, so they are recorded as producer questions.
They are **idempotent entries**: on re-run, update in place, never duplicate.

- **Q1 (scope / issue type).** Keep this as one `feature`, or re-type it to an
  `epic` and decompose into children at planning? The thirteen ACs span five
  independently testable subsystems (pairing resolver + data; field tier firing;
  owned tier persistence; fusion feedback/HUD; gym parity + docs + balance
  evidence).
  Options: (a) `epic` + children; (b) stay one `feature`; (c) split into two
  items (resolver + tiers, then feedback/parity/docs).
  **Recommended:** (a) `epic` — each subsystem has its own test gate and a
  single worktree session should not carry all five.
  — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (awaiting producer).

- **Q2 (where pairing data lives).** Author the pairing table in a new
  TypeScript module beside the catalogue (`src/utils/weaponEvolutions.ts`), or
  in designer-editable CSV/data (a new `src/data/weapon-pairings.csv` routed
  through `parseWeaponCatalogue`-style parsing, `src/utils/weaponCatalogue.ts`
  runtime guard and `src/core/weaponCatalogueStore.ts`)? AC2 says "catalogue
  data with a validating test" but the existing CSV is one row per weapon, so a
  pairing relation cannot be a column there.
  Options: (a) TS table in `src/utils/weaponEvolutions.ts`; (b) new CSV +
  parser + runtime guard; (c) TS now, CSV authoring as a follow-up item.
  **Recommended:** (a) — a cross-row relation read by one pure resolver, with
  compile-time id validation and no new CSV/parser/guard surface; designer
  authoring can follow as its own item once the three pairings prove out.
  — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (awaiting producer).

- **Q3 (hex matchup sequencing).** AC11 requires evolved weapons to classify as
  their base ids, but `resolveHexMatchup` does not exist yet (AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ
  is `open`/`plan_complete`). Options: (a) declare this item blocked by
  AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ; (b) publish the base ids from the resolver now and pin the
  classification test when that resolver lands (two-way cross-reference, no
  dependency); (c) implement matchup classification here.
  **Recommended:** (b) — base-id exposure is cheap and costs nothing now;
  blocking the whole evolution feature on a larger open item would stall it,
  while (c) would duplicate that item's work.
  — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (awaiting producer).

# Goal

As the implementation sessions, I want one **failing-until-implemented acceptance contract** for ship consumption and purchase auto-enable, so the two code slices that follow have a hard, executable definition of done rather than a matter of judgement.

## Context

Test-first verification slice of **AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF** (hex-battle consumption + equip-on-purchase). Producer answers: Q1 = C refined (all of the deployed ship's upgrades must be re-purchased, a purchase auto-enables), Q2 = B (win and loss both consume), Q3 = B (design change), Q4 = B (only the deployed ship is consumed).

Deliberately written against the **existing** public seams — `resolveHexCapture`, `resolveDeploymentDefeat`, `buy`, `purchaseHangarEntry`, `loadHangarWarPayload`/`saveHangarWarPayload`, `buildHangarScreenModel` — so the file compiles under `tsc --noEmit` while it is red (the repo type-checks `src`, so a test that imported a not-yet-existing export could not even be committed). The new reducer's own contract test belongs to the reducer item, not here.

## Scope

- New test file(s) under the hangar-war test area (for example `src/core/hangarWar/consumeOnBattleEnd.test.ts` and `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarPurchaseEquip.test.ts`), each test naming the AC it pins.
- Consumption (through `resolveHexCapture` and `resolveDeploymentDefeat`):
  - a win consumes the flown hull, the deployed starting weapons and the deployed modifiers; a loss consumes the same;
  - the free starter hull `hull-1` and starter weapon `spread` survive even when they were deployed;
  - owned items the player did not fly survive (hull, weapon, modifier, and their permanent level rows);
  - the consumed ids' `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` rows are deleted;
  - `activeHull` is the starter hull and `activeLoadout` is empty afterwards, and a subsequent deployment payload still builds (empty-loadout legality, AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D);
  - `bankedMinerals` / `bankedCores` are unchanged by consumption, and the win bonus still applies on a win;
  - a `campaignReset` (ring-end hangar falls) still produces the reset payload — consumption does not resurrect anything;
  - demo/attract runs never overwrite the player's war (the existing `_saveHangarWarPayload` guard).
- Auto-enable (through `purchaseHangarEntry`, plus the pure `buy` option):
  - a successful hull purchase sets `activeHull`; a weapon joins `activeLoadout.startingWeapons`; a modifier joins `activeLoadout.modifiers`;
  - a refused purchase (`owned` / `gated` / `unaffordable`) changes neither ownership nor the loadout;
  - `buy`'s default stays non-equipping (the A5/A6 rule survives for other callers).
- Gym↔game parity: the same assertions run through the headless seam (`GymHexWar.captureHex` / the pure resolvers), so no scene-only rule is required.
- Determinism: the same payload + deployment yields a deep-equal consumed payload.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test file exists for each contract (consumption on battle end; purchase auto-enable), each test naming the source AC.
- The consumption tests fail on today's tree (the flown ship is preserved) and the auto-enable tests fail on today's tree (`buying` grants ownership only).
- The tests compile cleanly under `npm run typecheck` while red, and every test runs against the pure core or the documented scene seam — no browser, no `localStorage` of the real player.
- The suite becomes fully green when the two implementation items land (they are the acceptance gate for both).
- `npm run build` stays clean (audio build + `tsc --noEmit` + vite build + bundle hygiene) for the test-only change.

- Automated tests cover both outcome paths and the purchase paths through the pure core and the scene seam (gym↔game parity): win and loss consumption, starter-kit survival, un-flown owned items surviving, consumed items' level rows removed, no soft-lock with an empty loadout, demo mode not overwriting the player's war, and auto-enable plus refusal for hull/weapon/modifier. (Restated verbatim from the parent item — this item is where that criterion is satisfied.)
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Key Files

- src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.test.ts — win/loss consumption assertions beside the existing resolver suite
- src/core/hangarWar/consumeOnBattleEnd.test.ts — the new focused consumption test file (suggested)
- src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarPurchaseEquip.test.ts — the new focused auto-enable test file (suggested)
- src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts — `purchaseHangarEntry` (system under test)
- src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts — payload round-trip / fixture builders
- src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts — the headless gym↔game parity seam

## Related work

- Parent: AH-0MWL5PAP2001XYYF
- Depends on: nothing
- Blocks: the pure reducer, the battle-end wiring and the auto-enable feature items

## Impact

The spend-the-ship loop and the buy-and-get-it loop are pinned by executable tests before either is built, so "the flown ship is spent" cannot be implemented by halves.
